migrations.name: 2026_10_03_01_migration_ledger
migrations.summary: Schema app_private and the ledger app_private.app_migrations(name, applied_at) that every later migration signs.

migrations.name: 2026_10_03_02_rpc_auth_null_guard
migrations.summary: adopt_swap, adopt_skip, decline_promote_request, approve_program and send_back_program refuse a caller without a user id; the two push warnings of the program-submit loop read as in production.

migrations.name: 2026_10_11_03_function_grants_lockdown
migrations.summary: No function of public is executable by anon or PUBLIC; a signed-in user executes an allow-list of 19 (the 12 helpers the policies call, the 7 RPCs the app calls); a function postgres creates later starts closed; all 36 functions run with search_path = public, pg_temp.

migrations.name: 2026_10_11_04_logged_history_guards
migrations.summary: A logged set (set_log_is_logged: done, failed, skipped, an RPE or an actual) or one with a video cannot be deleted, directly or by a cascade, from set_logs up to programs; exercise_slots.sets cannot go below one; a signed-in user's edit leaves the targets of a logged set as they were; adopt_swap and adopt_skip leave alone a slot with a logged set, a video or a comment; SET LOCAL app.allow_history_delete = 'on' lets a statement without a user id through.

migrations.name: 2026_10_11_05_students_role_gate
migrations.summary: No signed-in user inserts or deletes a students row, and none moves its link; every row written, by anyone, links a profile with the role coach to another one with the role student; exercise_library rows are added and edited by a coach only (is_coach()); the exercise of a slot and the substitute of a swap come from the library of the program's coach. The migration refuses to run (SLM05) while a link the gate would refuse exists.

migrations.name: 2026_10_11_06_pin_student_writes
migrations.summary: An athlete's own update of a set leaves its targets, its exercise, its number and is_student_added as they were; a session of a draft program carries no reviewed_at, archived_at, performed_at or scheduled_date, whoever writes it, and approve_program clears the four on the sessions of the program it approves; the author of a draft cannot change submitted_at once it is set.

migrations.name: 2026_10_11_07_profile_rules
migrations.summary: A new account gets a profile whose name is never empty: the name it was created with, else the part of its e-mail address before the @, else 'Athlete'; profiles.role stays what it was for a request that carries a user id and is written for one that does not (the SQL editor, the service-role key), except against a coach-athlete link: an athlete with a coach is not made a coach, a coach with athletes does not stop being one.

migrations.name: 2026_10_12_08_session_write_gates
migrations.summary: An athlete writes a set, a note on an exercise, a swap or a skip, and the video of a set — its row and its file — only in a session of the block being trained that the coach has neither archived nor reviewed (session_writable, session_writable_for_slot); reading stays open; a video is stored at <athlete>/<exercise slot of its set>/, so an account nobody coaches uploads nothing and nobody uploads under another athlete's exercise. A confirmed session that is not reviewed yet is still written.

migrations.name: 2026_10_13_09_review_lifecycle
migrations.summary: An athlete changes or takes back a confirmation only while its session is neither archived nor reviewed, and not while the review is being written; a signed-in user marks a session as reviewed, or sends feedback on it, only once its athlete has confirmed it (session_is_confirmed) — sessions reviewed without a confirmation before stay as they are and can still be confirmed; a confirmation, a swap or a skip that is taken back takes its unread coach notifications with it, and the ones that are stale today are deleted; the push of a confirmation is tagged by session.

migrations.name: 2026_10_13_10_goals_fk_coach_links
migrations.summary: A library exercise that a goal is set on cannot be deleted, nor the profile of a coach while an athlete is linked to it or a goal names it (goals.exercise_id, goals.coach_id and students.coach_id are ON DELETE RESTRICT); exercise_library has archived_at, which nothing reads yet; a coach reads the progress of a goal only while they coach its athlete (coach_profile_for_goal follows the link); transfer_student(athlete, new coach) moves the link and the athlete's goals together, for the owner of the database and the service role only.

migrations.name: 2026_10_13_11_activate_reorder_rpcs
migrations.summary: Three functions a signed-in user calls with the rights they already have (SECURITY INVOKER): activate_program(program) switches the athlete's other programs off and this one on in one statement, and refuses a draft and a program in the trash; reorder_sessions(phase, ids) and reorder_weeks(program, ids) renumber every session of a phase (0 to n-1) or every phase of a program (1 to n) in the order of the list, and refuse a list that is not exactly the children of the parent, archived sessions included. Nothing else: no table, no policy, no row.

migrations.name: 2026_10_13_12_copy_rpcs
migrations.summary: Four functions a signed-in user calls with the rights they already have (SECURITY INVOKER), each of which makes a whole copy or none: duplicate_session(session, title suffix) puts the copy right after its source; copy_sessions(ids, phase) adds one copy per entry at the end of a phase; duplicate_week(phase, program, label suffix) adds the phase with its sessions as the last phase of a program; duplicate_program(program, athlete, name suffix) makes an inactive block for the athlete or for another one of the coach. A copy is the prescription only — the targets of the sets, nothing that was trained — and leaves out, and counts, an exercise that is not in the library of the coach it is made for. Nothing else: no table, no policy, no row.

migrations.name: 2026_10_13_13_ensure_claim_rpcs
migrations.summary: Two functions a signed-in user calls, which run as their owner and ask who calls first (SECURITY DEFINER): ensure_set_logs(session) adds the prescribed sets that are missing in a session of the caller — read from the exercises as they are in the database, for its athlete only, in the block being trained, in a session neither archived nor reviewed — answers how many it added, and marks its INSERT with the transaction-local setting app.trusted_set_log_insert, which nothing reads yet; claim_push_subscription(endpoint, p256dh, auth, user agent) registers a device for the caller, and takes an endpoint over from another account only when the two keys sent are the ones stored with it. Nothing else: no table, no policy, no row.

migrations.name: 2026_10_13_14_table_grants_lockdown
migrations.summary: A request without a session holds no privilege on any table, view or sequence of public; a signed-in user holds SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on a table — what row-level security judges — and no longer TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER or MAINTAIN, and USAGE on a sequence; a table or a sequence postgres creates later in public starts with the same; the service role keeps everything. Nothing else: no table, no policy, no function, no row.

migrations.name: 2026_10_13_15_push_plumbing
migrations.summary: One function, send_push_event(recipient, payload, options), reads the vault and calls the send-push Edge Function through pg_net, with a time limit of 10 seconds and the bearer read from app_internal_bearer or, while the vault has none of that name, from app_service_role_key; the six notification triggers and the five coach RPCs that each carried a copy of that call ask it instead, inside their own EXCEPTION net, and send the same push as before; it is for the owner and the service role only. push_subscriptions.endpoint must be an https address at fcm.googleapis.com, updates.push.services.mozilla.com, a host under push.apple.com or one under notify.windows.com — validated when no row breaks it, otherwise for new and changed rows only. No row is changed.

migrations.name: 2026_10_13_16_rest_push_scheduling
migrations.summary: The end of a rest is scheduled in one request: schedule_rest_push(seconds, payload, endpoint) computes the time on the server, closes what the caller still had waiting, deletes the caller's rows older than 7 days and answers { id, fire_at, mode } — mode cron while a pg_cron job named sl-rest-push is active, edge otherwise; cancel_rest_push(id) takes it back. claim_rest_push(id), for the service role, is the one way a row gets sent: pending to sending, once, never for a row that was canceled or is more than a minute late. dispatch_due_rest_pushes(), which nothing calls until the optional job exists, closes the late rows and hands each row due within ten seconds to send-push once. scheduled_pushes has two more statuses (sending, expired) and two more columns (endpoint: the device the push is for; dispatched_at), an account names a device of its own only, and the rows that had been waiting for a time long past are closed — expired, or canceled where their athlete had asked. No row is deleted.

migrations.name: 2026_10_13_17_replay_grace_window
migrations.summary: A block stays open for its athlete for 72 hours after it is switched off, so that training logged without a connection is saved when the coach has activated the next block in between: programs.deactivated_at is the time is_active last went from true to false — written by the trigger trg_stamp_program_deactivated_at whichever way a block is switched off, cleared when it is switched on, and held against any other write that carries a user id — and program_active_for_session, which every write of an athlete asks, answers yes for a program out of the trash that is the active one or was switched off less than 72 hours ago. A block in the trash, a draft, and a session that is archived or reviewed stay closed. No row is written: a block switched off before the migration has no time, and no window.

migrations.name: 2026_10_13_18_retention
migrations.summary: One function, run_retention(), deletes the rows nobody reads any more and answers how many: rest pushes created more than 7 days ago — never one that is still to be sent —, notifications their recipient read more than 90 days ago, client errors older than 90 days. A notification that was never read stays, and no other table is named in it. It is for the owner of the database and the service role only, runs with the rights of its caller, and passes over a row another request holds instead of waiting for it. Nothing calls it: the owner does, once a month, or the nightly job of the optional migration 19. Applying the migration deletes no row.

migrations.name: 2026_10_13_19_pg_cron_jobs
migrations.summary: Where the extension pg_cron is switched on — the file refuses without it, and nothing is missing without the file — four jobs of pg_cron run as postgres: sl-rest-push calls dispatch_due_rest_pushes() every ten seconds, so that a rest push is handed to send-push by the database and schedule_rest_push answers mode cron; sl-retention calls run_retention() every night at 03:17 UTC; sl-push-failures calls record_push_failures() at seven minutes past every hour; sl-cron-history keeps three days of the runs pg_cron remembers. record_push_failures() is the one function it creates: for each hour that is over and in which a request the database sent through pg_net was not answered with a status between 200 and 299, it writes one line into client_errors with the role database — how many of how many, and what kind — and answers { hours, failed }; it is for the owner of the database and the service role only, and runs with the rights of its caller. No table, no column, no policy. From the first night on, what run_retention() deletes is deleted without anybody asking.

migrations.name: 2026_10_16_20_drafts_coach_readonly
migrations.summary: The phases, sessions, exercises and sets of a draft are written by its author alone: four triggers named block_draft_tree_write, on weeks, sessions, exercise_slots and set_logs, refuse (P0001, draft_read_only) a write that carries a user id other than the draft's author when the row belongs to a program whose status is draft — in the trash or not, its parent as it was and as it would be; a request without a user id, the author, and a row whose parent is gone (the cascade of a delete) go through. The row of the program is not judged: the coach still approves, sends back, renames, trashes and deletes a draft. approve_program marks the program approved first, then clears the four columns of its sessions as before, drops the sets without a target (prescribed, neither reps nor a duration, not logged, without a video) and adds the missing sets from the values of each exercise; it answers as before. No row is written.

migrations.name: 2026_10_16_21_rpe_half_steps_day_check
migrations.summary: set_logs.rpe is numeric(3,1), from 1 to 10 in steps of 0.5 (set_logs_rpe_check, written again for the new type, and set_logs_rpe_half_step); every RPE logged so far keeps its value. sessions.day_number is a weekday from 1 to 7 or nothing (sessions_day_number_weekday): the file first clears the values outside 1 to 7 and every weekday of a block an athlete wrote — drafts and approved blocks, trained sessions included; run after SET app.day_number_clearing = 'drafts', it keeps those of the approved blocks — and save_draft_tree writes a number outside 1 to 7 as no weekday instead of failing the whole tree. The weekdays it cleared do not come back with the rollback, which rounds an RPE in a half step away from zero.

migrations.name: 2026_10_16_22_client_errors_scope
migrations.summary: A client error is read by its author and by the coach of its author (students.coach_id); a line without an author — written by the database with the role database, or of an account that was deleted — by every coach: "Authors and their coach read client errors" replaces "Coaches read client errors", under which every coach read every line. trg_cap_client_errors, for a request that carries a user id, dates the line when it arrives and drops it without a word once the caller has 30 lines of the last hour; a request without a user id is not judged. Old lines are deleted by run_retention() of migration 18, not here. No row is written or deleted.
